title: Could we defend our training data sourcing if a rights holder challenged it?
description: A board-level oversight question testing whether an organisation has a documented, defensible record of where its generative model's training data came from, before a legal challenge forces the question.
question_text: Do we have a documented, defensible basis for the data used to train any generative model we deploy or procure — including a record of which sources were scraped, which were licensed, and what risk decision was made for each — or would we be assembling that record for the first time only after a rights holder's legal challenge, as in Getty Images v. Stability AI?
rationale: Getty Images v. Stability AI shows that a generative model's commercial deployment can be challenged years after launch over training-data sourcing decisions that were never documented at the time.
follow_up_actions: Request the current training data provenance log for any generative model developed or fine-tuned in-house.
For procured generative AI tools, ask the vendor what provenance documentation they can provide.
Confirm legal has reviewed the risk decisions recorded for any uncertain-provenance data source.

citations.title: Getty Images (US) Inc and others v Stability AI Limited [2025] EWHC 2863 (Ch)
citations.publisher: Courts and Tribunals Judiciary (England and Wales High Court)
